title: Nearest Tube / Subway Station Finder
description: Find nearby Underground-tagged station nodes and subway entrances in OpenStreetMap. Coverage and result limits apply.
summary_sentence: Results are limited to returned OpenStreetMap records and may omit closer or unmapped places. Confirm details with an authoritative local source.
quick_answer: The tool searches OpenStreetMap for mapped Underground-tagged station or subway entrance records around a chosen location, then sorts returned records by straight-line distance. It requests at most 300 records and displays up to 100, so it cannot guarantee the closest result or a complete list. Data, access and opening status can be incomplete or outdated.

The closest station may sit on the wrong line for your journey; the ranked list exists so the second and third — one stop further, direct line — are one glance away.

faq: Does it cover every rapid-transit type?
No. It searches station nodes whose network tag contains Underground and subway entrance nodes. Other station tagging and cities may be missed; entrances can appear separately.
Does it show lines and timetables?
No — stations and distances are this page's data. Lines, fares and live times belong to the transit operator's channels, which the station result helps you choose.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
You can search for a place instead of using device location. The selected search centre is sent to OpenStreetMap-based services for the lookup.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Station names change with sponsorships and renamings (occasionally infamous ones); the map record is one honest vintage of the name.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
Device location is optional. The selected coordinates are sent to Overpass to search; consult the privacy page for provider and site details.
The station exists but is not listed.
Entrances and stations are mapped unevenly; a brand-new station can lag. The operator's map settles a specific hunt.
Walking distance to the entrance?
The displayed distance is straight-line to the recorded station or entrance node, not a walking route.
Which station for the airport?
Rank from the airport's point — airport stations are recorded like others, and the list answers with the terminal's own context.
Night services?
A timetable question — the operator's night network map decides, not this one.
Stations under construction?
They enter the record as they open (or as planned entries in some data). A station you cannot enter is marked by reality at the gate — the operator confirms openings.
Interchange stations?
The query returns matching station nodes and entrances; it does not show lines or consolidate entrances into one station.
